title: Motor Learning & Neuroplasticity — How Patients Really Relearn Movement

hook.en: A perfect session in the gym can still fail at home. Learn how practice, feedback and repetition turn into lasting skill — after stroke and beyond.
hook.ur: Gym mein perfect session bhi ghar par fail ho sakta hai. Seekhein ke practice, feedback aur repetition kaise pakki skill banti hain — stroke ke baad aur us se aage bhi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll design practice that builds retention — choosing task-specific training, practice order, feedback and dose using the principles of neuroplasticity.
goal.ur: End tak aap aisi practice design kar sakenge jo retention banaye — neuroplasticity ke usoolon se task-specific training, practice ki tarteeb, feedback aur dose chun kar.

text.en: **Performance** is how well someone does during practice. **Learning** is the relatively permanent change that shows up later — in a **retention** test (days later) or a **transfer** test (a new situation, such as home). Many things that make practice look good actually reduce learning.
text.ur: **Performance** practice ke dauraan kitna acha karna hai. **Learning** woh nisbatan pakki tabdeeli hai jo baad mein dikhti hai — **retention** test mein (kuch din baad) ya **transfer** test mein (nayi situation, jaise ghar). Bohat si cheezein jo practice ko acha dikhati hain asal mein learning kam karti hain.

simpler.en: What matters is what the patient can still do next week at home — not how good it looked in the clinic today.
simpler.ur: Asal baat yeh hai ke patient agle hafte ghar par kya kar sakta hai — yeh nahi ke aaj clinic mein kitna acha dikha.

rows.en: Slow, effortful, many errors, needs to think
rows.ur: Aahista, mehnat se, bohat ghaltiyan, sochna parta hai

rows.en: Clear demonstration, simple cues, more frequent feedback
rows.ur: Wazeh demonstration, simple cues, zyada feedback
Kam ghaltiyan, movement ko behtar karna

rows.en: Vary practice, reduce feedback, let them self-correct
rows.ur: Practice badlein, feedback kam karein, khud correct karne dein

rows.en: Automatic, can do two things at once
rows.ur: Automatic, ek saath do kaam kar sakte hain
Dual-task aur asli duniya ki practice

text.en: **Practice order:** **blocked** practice (the same task repeated, A-A-A, B-B-B) gives good performance in the session. **Random** or variable practice (A-C-B, B-A-C) feels harder and looks worse — but usually gives **better retention and transfer**. This is the **contextual interference** effect.
text.ur: **Practice ki tarteeb:** **blocked** practice (ek hi kaam baar baar, A-A-A, B-B-B) session mein achi performance deti hai. **Random** ya variable practice (A-C-B, B-A-C) mushkil lagti hai aur buri dikhti hai — lekin aam tor par **behtar retention aur transfer** deti hai. Isay **contextual interference** effect kehte hain.

text.en: Learning to drive only in an empty car park, always the same circle, makes you great in that car park. Driving on different roads, at different times, with surprises, makes you a driver. Patients need the 'different roads' version before they go home.
text.ur: Sirf khaali parking mein, hamesha ek hi daira, gaari chalana seekhna aap ko us parking ka maahir bana deta hai. Mukhtalif sarkon par, mukhtalif waqt, surprises ke saath chalana aap ko driver banata hai. Patients ko ghar jane se pehle 'mukhtalif sarkon' wala version chahiye.

question.en: A patient after stroke practises sit-to-stand 30 times from the same plinth and does it perfectly. At home, from a low sofa, they can't. What principle was missed?
question.ur: Stroke ke baad patient ek hi plinth se 30 dafa sit-to-stand practise karta hai aur perfect karta hai. Ghar par neechay sofe se nahi kar pata. Kaun sa usool reh gaya?

text.en: Not enough repetitions
text.ur: Repetitions kam thin

feedback.en: 30 repetitions is reasonable — the problem was the lack of variety.
feedback.ur: 30 repetitions theek hain — masla variety ki kami tha.

text.en: Variable practice for transfer — different heights, surfaces and contexts
text.ur: Transfer ke liye variable practice — mukhtalif unchaiyan, surfaces aur context

feedback.en: Yes — blocked practice from one surface built performance, not transferable learning.
feedback.ur: Haan — ek surface se blocked practice ne performance banayi, transfer hone wali learning nahi.

text.en: Too much feedback was given
text.ur: Feedback zyada diya gaya

feedback.en: Possibly a factor, but the clearest gap is practice variability.
feedback.ur: Shayad ek wajah, lekin sab se wazeh kami practice ki variety hai.

text.en: **Feedback:** **knowledge of results (KR)** tells the outcome ('you stood up in 6 seconds'); **knowledge of performance (KP)** tells about the movement itself ('your trunk didn't lean forward enough'). Constant feedback creates dependence. **Fading** feedback, letting the learner ask for it, and summary feedback after several attempts support learning. An **external focus** ('push the floor away') usually beats an internal focus ('straighten your knee').
text.ur: **Feedback:** **knowledge of results (KR)** nateeja batata hai ('aap 6 second mein khare hue'); **knowledge of performance (KP)** movement ke baare mein batata hai ('aap ka trunk kaafi aage nahi jhuka'). Har waqt feedback dependence banata hai. Feedback ko **kam karte jana**, learner ko khud maangne dena, aur kai attempts ke baad summary feedback learning ki madad karte hain. **External focus** ('zameen ko door dhakelein') aam tor par internal focus ('apni knee seedhi karein') se behtar hai.

text.en: "Reach for the cup on the shelf"
text.ur: "Shelf par rakhe cup tak haath barhayein"

why.en: Focus on the goal in the environment.

text.en: "Lift your shoulder and extend your elbow"
text.ur: "Shoulder uthayein aur elbow seedhi karein"

text.en: "Step over the line on the floor"
text.ur: "Zameen par lagi line ke upar se qadam rakhein"

text.en: "Squeeze your gluteal muscles"
text.ur: "Apne gluteal muscles ko bheenchein"

text.en:
**Neuroplasticity principles** (Kleim & Jones) explain why this works. The brain changes with experience — for better or worse:
**Use it or lose it** · **Use it and improve it** · **Specificity** (you get better at what you practise) · **Repetition matters** · **Intensity matters** · **Time matters** · **Salience matters** (meaningful tasks) · **Age matters** · **Transference** and **interference**.
text.ur:
**Neuroplasticity ke usool** (Kleim & Jones) batate hain ke yeh kyun kaam karta hai. Dimagh tajurbe se badalta hai — achay ya bure ke liye:
**Use it or lose it** · **Use it and improve it** · **Specificity** (jo practise karein usi mein behtar) · **Repetition matters** · **Intensity matters** · **Time matters** · **Salience matters** (ba-maani kaam) · **Age matters** · **Transference** aur **interference**.

text.en:
In practice:
**Task-specific** — practise the actual goal (dressing, reaching, walking), not only isolated muscle work.
**High repetition** — a typical therapy session contains far fewer repetitions than learning needs; plan for hundreds, using circuits, groups and home programmes.
**Meaningful goals** — practise what matters to the patient (e.g. making tea, praying in sitting or standing).
**Prevent learned non-use** — encourage the affected limb in daily tasks.
text.ur:
Practice mein:
**Task-specific** — asal goal practise karein (kapre pehenna, haath barhana, chalna), sirf alag muscle kaam nahi.
**Zyada repetitions** — aam therapy session mein learning ki zaroorat se kaafi kam repetitions hoti hain; circuits, groups aur home programmes se saikron ki planning karein.
**Ba-maani goals** — woh practise karein jo patient ke liye aham ho (maslan chai banana, baith kar ya khare ho kar namaz parhna).
**Learned non-use rokein** — rozana ke kaamon mein affected limb istemal karne ki targheeb dein.

text.en: Evidence: across stroke rehabilitation trials, more therapy time is associated with better outcomes (dose–response; Lohse 2014). Observational studies show typical sessions often include only dozens of repetitions of a task — far below what animal and human learning studies suggest is needed. Task-specific, repetitive practice is central to current stroke guidelines.
text.ur: Evidence: stroke rehabilitation trials mein zyada therapy time behtar nataij se juda hai (dose–response; Lohse 2014). Observational studies dikhati hain ke aam sessions mein aksar kisi kaam ki sirf darjanon repetitions hoti hain — jo animal aur human learning studies ki zaroorat se kaafi kam hai. Task-specific, repetitive practice aaj ki stroke guidelines ka markaz hai.

question.en: Which plan best applies the principles of neuroplasticity for a patient relearning reaching after stroke?
question.ur: Stroke ke baad reaching dobara seekhne wale patient ke liye kaun sa plan neuroplasticity ke usool behtareen apply karta hai?

text.en: 10 passive range-of-motion movements, three times a week
text.ur: Hafte mein teen dafa 10 passive range-of-motion movements

feedback.en: Passive movement has a role, but it isn't active, repetitive or task-specific.
feedback.ur: Passive movement ka kirdaar hai, lekin yeh active, repetitive ya task-specific nahi.

text.en: Hundreds of active reaches daily to real objects at varied heights, with home practice
text.ur: Rozana saikron active reaches asli cheezon tak, mukhtalif unchaiyon par, ghar ki practice ke saath

feedback.en: Yes — specific, repetitive, intense, varied and meaningful.
feedback.ur: Haan — specific, repetitive, intense, mukhtalif aur ba-maani.

text.en: Electrical stimulation alone
text.ur: Sirf electrical stimulation

feedback.en: Stimulation can be an adjunct, but without active task practice it won't build skill.
feedback.ur: Stimulation madadgar ho sakti hai, lekin active task practice ke baghair skill nahi banti.

text.en: Common mistakes: correcting every single attempt; only blocked practice on one surface; judging success by the session instead of retention; and letting therapy become mostly rest and talk — the clock runs, but few repetitions happen.
text.ur: Aam ghaltiyan: har attempt ko correct karna; sirf ek surface par blocked practice; kamyabi ko retention ke bajaye session se judge karna; aur therapy ko zyada tar aaram aur baaton mein badal dena — ghari chalti rehti hai, lekin repetitions kam hoti hain.

question.en: Your patient is in the associative stage of learning to walk with a stick. Which feedback approach fits best?
question.ur: Aap ka patient stick ke saath chalna seekhne ke associative stage mein hai. Kaun sa feedback tareeqa behtar hai?

text.en: Correct every step out loud
text.ur: Har qadam par bol kar correct karein

feedback.en: Constant feedback makes them dependent on you.
feedback.ur: Musalsal feedback unhein aap par mohtaaj banata hai.

text.en: Let them walk a few lengths, then give brief summary feedback or ask how they think it went
text.ur: Kuch lengths chalne dein, phir mukhtasar summary feedback dein ya poochein ke unke khayal mein kaisa raha

feedback.en: Yes — reduced, summary and learner-requested feedback builds self-correction.
feedback.ur: Haan — kam, summary aur learner ke maangne par feedback khud correct karna sikhata hai.

text.en: Give no information at all
text.ur: Bilkul koi maloomat na dein

feedback.en: Some feedback is still needed; the trick is how much and when.
feedback.ur: Kuch feedback phir bhi chahiye; asal baat kitna aur kab hai.

text.en: **Make it Specific, Repetitive, Varied and Meaningful — then step back.** (SRVM: fade your feedback as they learn.)
text.ur: **Specific, Repetitive, Varied aur Meaningful banayein — phir peeche hat jayein.** (SRVM: seekhne ke saath feedback kam karein.)

summary.en: Judge learning by retention and transfer, not in-session performance; variable practice beats blocked practice for learning.
summary.ur: Learning ko retention aur transfer se judge karein, session ki performance se nahi; learning ke liye variable practice blocked se behtar.

summary.en: Use external-focus cues and faded, summary feedback; constant feedback creates dependence.
summary.ur: External-focus cues aur kam hota, summary feedback istemal karein; musalsal feedback dependence banata hai.

summary.en: Neuroplasticity needs specific, repetitive, intense and meaningful practice — plan for far more repetitions than a typical session gives.
summary.ur: Neuroplasticity ko specific, repetitive, intense aur ba-maani practice chahiye — aam session se kahin zyada repetitions plan karein.

back.en: Performance = during practice; learning = relatively permanent change seen on retention or transfer tests.
back.ur: Performance = practice ke dauraan; learning = nisbatan pakki tabdeeli jo retention ya transfer tests par dikhe.

front.en: What is the contextual interference effect?

back.en: Random/variable practice lowers in-session performance but improves retention and transfer compared with blocked practice.
back.ur: Random/variable practice session ki performance kam karti hai lekin blocked ke muqable retention aur transfer behtar.

back.en: Knowledge of results = outcome; knowledge of performance = quality of the movement.
back.ur: Knowledge of results = nateeja; knowledge of performance = movement ka maiyaar.

front.en: Name five Kleim & Jones neuroplasticity principles.
front.ur: Kleim & Jones ke paanch neuroplasticity usool?

back.en: Any five: use it or lose it, use it and improve it, specificity, repetition, intensity, time, salience, age, transference, interference.
back.ur: Koi paanch: use it or lose it, use it and improve it, specificity, repetition, intensity, time, salience, age, transference, interference.

note.en: Practice and feedback in more depth.
note.ur: Practice aur feedback mazeed tafseel se.

note.en: Putting task-specific practice into a full plan.
note.ur: Task-specific practice ko mukammal plan mein dalna.
